record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: Find additional Banach spaces X with the following property: whenever X is a subspace of a Banach space Z and the quotient Z/X is isomorphic to X, the subspace X is complemented in Z.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a Banach space $X$ a "self-quotient complemented" space if it has the following property: whenever $X$ embeds as a closed subspace of a Banach space $Z$ such that the quotient $Z/X$ is (linearly topologically) isomorphic to $X$, then $X$ is complemented in $Z$ (that is, there is a bounded linear projection from $Z$ onto $X$).

Known examples include certain classical sequence spaces. The task is: exhibit additional Banach spaces $X$ enjoying this property. More precisely, identify and prove new (classes of) Banach spaces $X$ such that every short exact sequence
$$0 \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow Z \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow 0$$
in the category of Banach spaces and bounded linear operators splits.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open-ended research question asking for additional examples of Banach spaces with the stated self-quotient splitting property. General searches reveal no definitive classification; the question of when extensions $0\to X\to Z\to X\to 0$ split is part of the active study of Ext groups in the Banach-space category, with only partial results known.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing when subspaces of Banach spaces are complemented; no general classification of self-quotient complemented spaces is given.
status_evidence.claim: The literature contains only partial results on when subspaces are complemented in larger Banach spaces, supporting that the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Complemented subspace - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Lindenstrauss-Tzafriri: every infinite-dimensional non-Hilbert Banach space contains an uncomplemented closed subspace.
status_evidence.claim: General complementation phenomena in Banach spaces remain subtle and a complete classification for the self-quotient property is not known.
